results.name: the 1KX5 nucleosome's DNA, rebuilt from its own parameters in place, puts the crystal's bases back (base-atom RMSD <= 0.1 A, no superposition)
the 1KX5 DNA follows a left-handed superhelix of the published radius and pitch (Richmond & Davey 2003: 41.9 A and 25.9 A; within 1.5 A and 3 A)
DNA bend angles measured on the crystal structures match the published bends (TBP 80, CAP 90 deg within 15 deg; IHF more than 160 deg, measured >= 145 deg)
the 6HKT array is a two-start zigzag: six nucleosomes, each nearer the nucleosome two along the DNA than its neighbour (mean centre distances)

in the Dip-C single-cell structures, gene-rich chromosomes sit nearer the centre of the nucleus: chromosome 19 is more central than 18 in at least 5 of 6 cells, and radial position falls with gene density (Spearman rho <= -0.5)
